reports.subject: PERIMETER INTRUSION DETECTION ACTIVATION, SECTOR 4
reports.reported_status: Closed. Cause identified and corrected. No indication of attempted penetration.
reports.text:
E01-SS-R01
REPORT ID:  E01-SS-R01
SERIAL:     NSAAR-PSD-0463
PRECEDENCE: ROUTINE
DTG:        032311K SEP 26
FROM:       Physical Security Division, Perimeter Watch
TO:         Installation Watch Officer, BDOC, NSA AMBER REACH
INFO:       Security Department Duty Chief
SUBJ:       PERIMETER INTRUSION DETECTION ACTIVATION, SECTOR 4
REF:        (a) ARI 5510.7B

1. SITUATION. At 2258K the perimeter intrusion detection system generated a Zone 4-B activation on the seaward fence line south of Tower 2.
2. DETAILS. Reaction force arrived on scene at 2303K and walked the affected fence panels and the adjacent clear zone under lights. Fence fabric, outriggers, and tension wire intact. No cut, climb, or lift signature. No footprints in the graded strip. Tower 2 reports no observation of movement inside or outside the clear zone during the period.
3. ASSESSMENT. Activation is attributed to spray-driven salt accumulation shorting the sensor cable termination at post 4-19 during the onshore gusts recorded between 2230K and 2255K. Zone 4-B has recorded five weather-attributed activations in the past forty days, all similarly adjudicated, and the termination at post 4-19 accounts for three of them.
4. ACTIONS TAKEN. Termination cleaned, dried, and re-sealed. Zone reset and functionally tested end to end at 2306K. Sector 4 restored to full detection. Corrosion work order PWD-7801 opened against post 4-19.
5. STATUS. Closed. Cause identified and corrected. No indication of attempted penetration.
6. POC. MA1 R. Tomasek, Perimeter Watch Supervisor, x4412.

reports.text:
E01-SS-R06
REPORT ID:  E01-SS-R06
SERIAL:     NSAAR-CSER-0043
PRECEDENCE: PRIORITY
DTG:        040301K SEP 26
FROM:       Communications Security Equipment Readiness Cell, Building 14
TO:         Installation Watch Officer, BDOC, NSA AMBER REACH
INFO:       Communications Security Material Custodian; COMSEC Equipment
            Maintenance Section; SAG SENTINEL Communications Officer
SUBJ:       SERVICE-LIFE REPLACEMENT EXECUTED IN THE SIX KEY TRANSFER
            DEVICES ISSUED TO SAG SENTINEL FOR ROTATION 26-04
REF:        (a) ARI 5510.7B
            (b) ARI 2280.1A
            (c) Caldera Integrated Systems Product Advisory CIS-PA-26-047
            (d) Caldera Integrated Systems Cell Certification Data Sheet
                CIS-CDS-28-A
            (e) Building 14 Maintenance Job 26-0413

1. SITUATION. This cell has consolidated the equipment maintenance record and the pre-sail issue record for the KL-9 key transfer devices issued to SAG SENTINEL for Operation TIDEWALL rotation 26-04. Six devices are aboard the four units of the group. The KRC-2 cells in all six were replaced at a certified maintenance activity on 1-2 September, before issue, and the certified service life of the cells now fitted in them ends at 0001Z, 4 March 2027.
2. EQUIPMENT. The KRC-2 cell is the internal power source of a KL-9 key transfer device. It is what maintains the device's loaded key material and its tamper-response circuit between uses. Reference (c) fixes the certified service life of the KRC-2 cells originally fitted in production lot 27-D at 0001Z, 7 September 2026 and directs their replacement before that date. Cell replacement requires the device to be opened at a certified maintenance activity by the regional technical representative; it cannot be performed by a unit or by the custodian.
3. REPLACEMENT EXECUTED. The regional technical representative, Mr. D. Halvorsen of Caldera Integrated Systems, arrived at Amber Reach on 1 September on curtailed travel, his prior tasking having overrun. In the maintenance bay hours available to him he executed reference (c) against the six devices designated for issue by issue plan TIDEWALL 26-04 — KTD-812, KTD-815, KTD-819, KTD-823, KTD-826, and KTD-831 — the deploying set having been sequenced first by direction of the COMSEC Equipment Maintenance Section. Each of the six was opened, re-celled, closed, and passed post-maintenance test. The six post-maintenance test records are filed under reference (e), signed by the representative and by CTM1 P. Gundersen at 021640K. The configuration record was updated at 021702K and cell stock was reconciled and dual-signature verified with the custodian at 021715K.
4. SERVICE LIFE OF THE CELLS NOW FITTED. The cells fitted in the six devices are KRC-2 cells of cell production lot 28-A. Reference (d) fixes their certified service life at 0001Z, 4 March 2027. Rotation 26-04 is programmed as a nine-day rotation and the group is programmed to return to Amber Reach on its completion. The certified service life of the cells now fitted therefore ends approximately six months after the group returns, and no service-life or other maintenance action falls due on any of the six devices during the rotation.
5. ISSUE. Devices KTD-812, KTD-815, KTD-819, KTD-823, KTD-826, and KTD-831 were drawn from Container C-7 against issue plan TIDEWALL 26-04 and issued between 0145K and 0212K, 4 September: three to USS BRENNAN and one each to USS ASHFORD, USS KETTLEWELL, and USNS PALO DUNE. This cell compared the six serials on the issue receipts against the six serials on the reference (e) post-maintenance test records at 0248K. The two sets match device for device, and no device that had not been re-celled was drawn or issued. Receipts are dual-signed, container seals and inventory reconcile, nothing is unaccounted for, and every device passed its startup self-test at issue. No person outside the appointed chain handled any device at any point.
6. DEVICES REMAINING ASHORE. Ten lot 27-D devices remain ashore and have not been re-celled. Their replacement is scheduled for the availability of 9-10 September, at which the representative returns; replacement cells for all ten are on hand in Building 14 and are inventoried and reserved against the requirement. All ten are restricted from issue until the replacement is executed, and none is issued to any unit or held by any unit. Reference (c) is closed in the maintenance record against the six devices aboard and remains open against the ten ashore.
7. ACTIONS TAKEN. Maintenance and issue records cross-checked, matched by serial, and preserved. SAG SENTINEL Communications Officer informed at 0256K that the six devices aboard carry lot 28-A cells certified to 0001Z, 4 March 2027. Ten ashore devices restricted from issue. Copies of the reference (e) test records and the reference (d) data sheet forwarded to the Communications Security Material Custodian at 0258K.
8. STATUS. Closed. The service-life replacement directed by reference (c) was executed and post-maintenance tested on all six devices before they were issued, and the cells now fitted in them are certified past the end of rotation 26-04. No service-life action is outstanding against any device issued to SAG SENTINEL.
9. POC. CWO3 M. Lachance, Communications Security Equipment Readiness Cell, x4488.

REF:        (a) Maintenance Ticket NSAAR-IT-12244

1. SITUATION. At 0058K, sixteen administrative telephone extensions in Building 3 lost dial tone.
2. DETAILS. The Network Operations Center traced the loss to a failed line card in shelf 2 of the Building 3 administrative switch. The card was reseated without effect and replaced from spares at 0112K. All sixteen extensions were tested and restored by 0116K. The affected extensions are unclassified administrative lines only; no operational, secure, or emergency circuit is carried on that shelf, and the installation's secure voice and data circuits are on separate equipment in a separate building that was unaffected.

4. ACTIONS TAKEN. Card replaced and returned for failure analysis. Ticket NSAAR-IT-12244 closed. Refresh request annotated.
5. STATUS. Closed. Cause identified and service restored.
6. POC. IT2 G. Brantley, Network Operations Center Watch, x4390.

            ROTATION 26-04
REF:        (a) OPORD TIDEWALL, Annex K
            (b) Talaveras Maritime Safety Authority Notice to Mariners
                TAL-26-247

1. SITUATION. SAG SENTINEL departure from NSA Amber Reach has been retimed from 0530K, 4 September, to 050200K, 5 September, in execution of Operation TIDEWALL rotation 26-04.
2. DETAILS. Reference (b), received at 0305K, closes the eastern Verrick Strait outbound traffic lane from 040600K to 042200K, 4 September, for a host-nation hydrographic survey of reported shoaling north of Talaveras Light. Commander Task Group directed the retiming at 0309K. All communications material and key transfer devices required for the rotation are to be aboard assigned units not later than 050115K; the six key transfer devices already issued remain aboard their units and no return to Building 14 is required. Sea and anchor detail is set at 050130K.
3. ASSESSMENT. No alternate communications material package is prepared or available at Amber Reach, and none is required. The Communications Security Equipment Readiness Cell reported at 0301K that the service-life replacement on all six issued devices was executed and post-maintenance tested before issue and that the cells fitted are certified to 0001Z, 4 March 2027, which is past the end of the rotation. No issued device requires withholding, exchange, or return to the Building 14 maintenance bay, and no maintenance action stands between the group and the retimed departure.
4. ACTIONS TAKEN. Revised departure timeline issued. Units notified of the 050115K deadline. Sea and anchor bill reposted. Reference (b) promulgated to SAG SENTINEL units and Port Operations.
5. STATUS. Departure retimed to 050200K, 5 September. Issued communications material cleared for the rotation.
